search_log: Searched "Lessons in Chemistry" Bonnie Garmus excerpt, first chapter, publisher, and Google Books; opened the Penguin Books Australia authorized extract and the Penguin Random House title page.

Searched "Lessons in Chemistry" with point of view, third person, narrator, multiple narrators, and alternating point of view; opened the Audible author interview, GradeSaver literary-elements page, and BookRags POV answer.

Searched for interior and Six-Thirty excerpts. Bookreporter surfaced Chapters 1 and 3 but timed out when opened; The StoryGraph only described an Apple Books Chapters 1-5 excerpt and did not expose the prose.

Searched the exact apparent first-person exceptions. The fuller context of "I used to tell myself every day was new" identifies Calvin as the speaker, while "People like my father preach love" occurs inside Elizabeth's extended dialogue.
No opened source indicated sustained first- or second-person base sections; multiple viewpoints were consistently character focalizations within third-person narration.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third person, moving omnisciently or through multiple character focalizers, including Six-Thirty. Numerous Goodreads event passages independently expose external access to Elizabeth's, Calvin's, Madeline's, and Six-Thirty's thoughts, agreeing with the authorized Penguin opening and whole-book POV descriptions. The two clipped first-person event quotes are local speech by Calvin and Elizabeth when restored to context, so they do not create alternating narration. The main scope limitation is that the Tier A extract covers only the opening, but this is offset by many interior quote passages, the author's whole-book account of ten focal viewpoints, and two explicit whole-book third-person descriptions; no credible contrary structure was found.
